en: Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Exhortation 28.
The Training Rule on Boarding a Boat:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group of six monks, having made an appointment with the bhikkhunīs, boarded a boat together.
People criticized, grumbled, and complained, saying:
"Just as we, together with our wives, enjoy ourselves on a boat, even so these recluses, sons of the Sakyans, having made an appointment with the bhikkhunīs, enjoy themselves on a boat."
The monks heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those monks who were of few desires... [and so forth]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized, saying:
"How can the group-of-six monks, having made an arrangement with the bhikkhunīs, board a single boat?"... [and so forth]...
“Is it true, monks, that you boarded a single boat in concert with the bhikkhunīs?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before] ...
"How indeed, you foolish men, can you embark upon a single boat in concert with the bhikkhunīs?
This, foolish men, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:"
“Whatever monk, having made an appointment with a nun, should board the same boat—whether going upstream or downstream—there is an offense of expiation.
Thus was this training rule laid down by the Blessed One for the monks.
Now at that time, a number of monks and nuns were traveling along the highway from Sāketa to Sāvatthī.
On the way, a river had to be crossed.
Then those bhikkhunīs said this to the bhikkhus:
“We too shall cross over together with you, venerable sirs.”
“Sister, it is not permitted for a bhikkhunī to board a single boat in concert with [a man], saying:
‘Either you cross first, or we shall cross.
‘Venerable sir, these noble ladies are the foremost of persons.’”
“Venerable ladies, please cross first.
But as those bhikkhunīs were crossing later, robbers robbed them and raped them.
Then those bhikkhunīs went to Sāvatthī and reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs.
The bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhus.
The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, having given a discourse on the Dhamma with reference to this cause and this occasion, addressed the bhikkhus:
“I allow you, monks, for the purpose of crossing over, to board a single boat in company with a bhikkhunī.
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule thus:

‘Whatever monk, having made an appointment with a bhikkhunī, should board a single boat, whether going upstream or downstream, except for the purpose of crossing over, there is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).’”
"But whoever" means whoever such a person... "a bhikkhu" means... [as before].
...pe... this is the meaning intended here by the term "bhikkhu.
A "bhikkhunī" is one who has received full ordination in both Saṅghas.
"Together" means on one side.
"Having arranged" means...

“If one makes an appointment, saying, ‘Sister, let us ride together,’ ‘Venerable sir, let us ride together,’ ‘Venerable sir, let us ride together,’ or ‘Sister, let us ride together,’ whether today, yesterday, or tomorrow,” there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If the monk rides after the nun has already ridden, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If the nun rides after the monk has already ridden, there is an offense of expiation.
If both board together, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Going upstream" means traveling upriver.
"Going downwards" refers to the flow of vital energy (*ojā*).
"Except for crossing sideways" means...
Except for crossing over horizontally.
In a village where a cock can fly from one house to another, for each interval between houses, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
In a forest that is not near a village, for every half-yojana, there is an offense of expiation.

If he makes an appointment and, perceiving that an appointment has been made, boards a single boat going upstream or downstream—except for crossing transversely—he commits an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
If he makes an appointment and, being in doubt, boards a single boat going upstream or downstream—except for crossing transversely—he commits an offense entailing expiation.

If he makes an appointment and, perceiving that no appointment has been made, boards a single boat going upstream or downstream—except for crossing transversely—he commits an offense entailing expiation.
If the monk makes an appointment and the nun does not, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she has not made an appointment but he perceives that she has, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If she has not made an appointment but he is uncertain of it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it has not been prepared, and he perceives that it has not been prepared,
there is no offense. There is no offense in crossing over horizontally.
They board without having made an appointment;
the nun makes an appointment, but the monk does not;
they board without a prior agreement.
In times of distress,
for one who is insane,
and for a first offender.
The eighth training rule concerning boarding a boat is finished.
